entry.title: Unconventional charge density wave order in ErTe$_{3}$: symmetry breakings and fluctuations probed by Raman scattering
entry.summary:
Recent experiments have revealed unexpected mirror-symmetry breakings in the charge density-wave (CDW) state of rare-earth tritellurides, suggesting a putative ferro-axial CDW state. Here we report polarization-resolved Raman scattering measurements tracking the point-group symmetry breakings across the CDW phase transition in the rare-earth tritelluride ErTe$_3$. We show that the mirror-symmetry breakings follow closely the emergence of the CDW order, suggesting a single component CDW order parameter.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science

entry.title: Ginzburg-Landau Theory with Elastic Incompatibility Describes the Liquid-G-phase-Crystal State Diagram
entry.summary:
We derive a mechanically consistent Ginzburg-Landau theory for the metastable heterogeneous G state reported in deeply undercooled metallic liquids. The central result is that type-II-like mixed-state physics can emerge structurally with the random internal stress field playing the role of the magnetic field. Frozen eigenstrain due to elastic incompatibility between ordered cores and the amorphous matrix generates incompatible stress, while the non-affine internal strain in the liquid-like matrix in between the ordered cores relaxes that stress over a finite screening length $λ_σ$ (analogous to the London length in the superconducting problem).

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science #rust

entry.title: Majorana Edge-to-bound State Transition in Interferometric Superconductor Rings
entry.summary:
Manipulating flux quanta in topological superconductors is central to vortex braiding in quantum computing. Their interferometric superconducting rings can host either topologically protected edge states with fluxes confined inside the central hollow area or vortex bound states in flux cores at the annulus walls. Here we demonstrate a strategy to drive topological edge states into vortex bound states by tuning the relative scale of vortex size and annulus width in nano-ring interferometric device on 2M-WS$_2$ topological superconductor.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science #distributed-systems

entry.title: Tensor Networks for Materials Simulation and Quantum Chemistry
entry.summary:
Predicting the properties of correlated materials and molecules often requires a many-body description that goes beyond single-particle and mean-field approximations. Tensor networks address this challenge by exploiting the entanglement structure of quantum states to construct compact, systematically improvable representations. Although developed largely for idealized model Hamiltonians, these methods are increasingly being integrated into material-specific calculations.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science #infosec

entry.title: First- and Second-Order Electron Position Correlators Reveal Topological Phase Transitions
entry.summary:
The theory of conventional critical phenomena is built around the concepts of fluctuations and correlators of local observables. Here, we show that topological phase transitions can also be characterized through spatial and temporal two-point correlation functions associated with fluctuations of the electronic position operator. The key object is the antisymmetric part of the position-position correlation function, which yields the Chern number in the equal-time and equal-space limit.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science

entry.title: The Merck/Moderna Results
entry.summary:
This is one of those times - and there are many - when you should evaluate a biopharma news story based on the science and not on the stock market. I’m referring to the clinical trial data that Merck and Moderna released yesterday for their vaccine (intismeran autogene)/Keytruda combination in melanoma patients after surgery. That should probably read “released under duress”, because the data leaked in advance of a meeting presentation, and the companies were more or less forced to press-release on the numbers.

Source: In the Pipeline (Derek Lowe — Drug Discovery & Chemistry) · Tags: #genomics-proteins #materials-science
